summary: Franz Aubrey Metcalf is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Chicago and worked as an instructor at California State University, Los Angeles (attested 2002–2006).

Franz Bernhard (1931–1971) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ernst Waldschmidt and completed his habilitation at Goethe University Frankfurt. In 1966, he became Professor and Seminar Director at the University of Hamburg.

Franz Bopp (1791–1867) was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, Karl Joseph Hieronymus Windischmann, and Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. He served as Chair of Sanskrit at Humboldt University of Berlin (1821–1867).

Franz Heinrich Trithen (1820–1854) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. After studying under Franz Bopp in Berlin, he worked at the British Museum (c. 1844–1848) and as Professor of Modern Languages at Oxford (c. 1848–1854).

Franz Kielhorn (1840–1908) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at Deccan College (1866) and later Professor of Sanskrit at Göttingen (c. 1881–1908).

Franz Xaver Erhard is a Tibetologist. He completed master's degrees at the Free University of Berlin and Humboldt University of Berlin, and earned his Ph.D. from the University of Bonn (attested 2003).

Franz-Karl Ehrhard (born 1953) is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctorate under Lambert Schmithausen. He directed the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (1988–1993) and served as a professor at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (2006–2012).
François Gros (1933–2021) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Lyon (c. 1951–1956). He later held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (c. 1977–2002).
François Jacob (1920–2013) studied at Lycée Carnot and the Paris Medical Faculty (c. 1938–1947). He held a post at the Collège de France from 1964 to 1991.

Françoise Pommaret (born 1954) specializes in Tibetology and history/archaeology. Educated at INALCO and the University of Paris, she served as a lecturer at INALCO and became Directeur de recherche at the CNRS in 2002.
Françoise Robin (born 1968) is a scholar of Tibetology who studied under Heather Stoddard. She held a post at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales around 2005.
Fred Pfeil (1949–2005) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields who studied at Amherst College (c. 1967–1971). He later held a post at Oregon State University.
Frederick M. Asher (1941–2021) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He spent his career at the University of Minnesota, serving as Professor from approximately 1971 to 2021.

Frederick William Thomas (1867–1956) was an Indologist and Tibetologist educated at Trinity College, Cambridge. He served as Librarian at the India Office Library (c. 1903–1927) and Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1927–1937).

Frederik David Kan Bosch (1887–1967) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He headed the Archaeological Service in the Netherlands East Indies (c. 1916–1936) before holding posts at Utrecht University (1938–1945) and Leiden University (1946–1957).

Fredrik Barth (1928–2016) studied at Chicago and Cambridge under Edmund Leach. He held academic posts at Bergen (c. 1961–1974), Oslo (c. 1974–1985), Emory (c. 1989–2008), Harvard (c. 1989–1996), and Boston University (c. 1997–2008).

Friederike Assandri is a scholar in Sinology and religious studies. She pursued her doctoral studies under Gunther-Dietz Sontheimer at Heidelberg University, where she also held an affiliation attested in 2013.

Friedhelm Hardy (1943–2004) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He served at King's College London (c. 1975–2004) and was the Wilde Lecturer in Comparative Religion at the University of Oxford (1985–1987).

Friedrich Alexander Bischoff (1928–2009) was a scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Paris and served as Professor of Sinology at the University of Hamburg (c. 1976–1981).

Friedrich August Rosen (1805–1837) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Bopp. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at University College London (c. 1828–1836) and Professor of Sanskrit at the University of London (1834).
